title: Cross-Team Readiness Signals and Roadmap Handoff Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Roadmap handoffs between Product, Eng, Design, and Security are currently managed by ad-hoc Slack threads and status spreadsheets. This creates noisy cutovers, unclear ownership of upstream blockers, and reactive escalation shortly before milestones.

Goal: Define a lightweight, telemetry-driven readiness signal and explicit handoff protocol that: 1) provides a single source of truth for whether an initiative is ready to enter the next cycle phase (Discovery -> Spec -> Implementation -> Release), 2) surfaces cross-team blockers early, and 3) provides an escalation timeline and playbook that reduces last-minute emergency work.

Scope: This ticket defines the signal set, gating thresholds, handoff checklist, escalation windows, and the minimum observable events to be emitted by Eng/Design/Security. Implementation of the signal ingestion pipeline (dashboard + alerting) will be a follow-on engineering ticket.

Out-of-scope: Full automation of gate enforcement and automatic rollbacks. Deep integration with external issue trackers beyond linking (e.g., full two-way sync) is deferred.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented readiness signal model exists and is approved by Eng, Design, and Security leads.
2) A public handoff checklist (Confluence) with required artifacts per phase and owner for each artifact.
3) A set of telemetry events and Slack alert rules are specified so that missing artifacts or blocked status trigger a notification at T-14d and T-3d before phase cutover.
4) A one-page escalation playbook is published with named contacts and SLA for acknowledgment.
5) Pilot run scheduled with two initiatives in Cycle 2026-Q2 and success criteria defined (reduction in last-minute tasks, measured in retrospective).
notes: Principles: lightweight, visible, actionable. Avoid adding bureaucratic gates — prefer signals that are easy to emit and reason about.

Proposed signal categories: artifact_presence (PRs, Specs, UX mocks), infra_readiness (staging infra, dedicated GPU pool reservations), security_clearance (threat model completed, KMS integration approved), performance_baseline (latency + cost guardrail tests).
Each signal should have three states: green (ready), amber (at risk, with reason), red (blocked). The amber state should include an auto-expiring note with next action/owner.

We will standardize a short event payload that teams can emit into the telemetry bus; engineering will map this to a dashboard card and to Slack digest. Example event: 'readiness.event: {initiative_key, phase, signal_name, status, owner, evidence_url, timestamp}'. (Teams will send as a flat JSON string in telemetry; implementation ticket will define exact schema.)
Landing pages: Confluence spec (link below), pilot onboarding checklist, and a playbook template for SRE/Security involvement.

risks: Risk: Teams may treat signals as binary pass/fail and compress nuanced engineering risk into a single flag. Mitigation: require an 'explainers' field for amber/red states and run a training session during pilot onboarding.
Risk: Telemetry ingestion work may slip and delay pilot. Mitigation: allow manual 'submit readiness' fallback and log provenance so ingestion can be swapped in later.
Risk: Over-alerting. Mitigation: aggregate alerts into a daily digest and only escalate persistent reds according to the escalation cadence.
